evidence.why: Parent attack-state setup and its thin movement adapter.
Child physics has a distinct stage-line movement implementation.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes the main Ho-Oh attack-state physics adapter from the Sacred Fire child's stage-line-following physics callback. It also agrees with the supported parent animation hypothesis itHouou_Attack_Anim without claiming recovery of an original symbol.

evidence.why: Command is cleared before the spawn attempt.
Exact query endpoints, short-circuit condition and child dereference.

facts.rationale: Corrects the upward-query description and preserves short-circuit ordering, the no-hit branch and the unchecked allocation-result dereference.
facts.value: Called after the parent accessory callback clears a nonzero second animation-command variable. It first queries the vertical segment from Ho-Oh's saved release position to the bottom blast-zone boundary. Only if that query fails does it query from the top blast-zone boundary to the saved release position. If both fail, it performs no spawn. On a successful query it requests one Sacred Fire child, then immediately stores the returned stage-line identifier in the child's houou.timer field without a local null check on the spawn result.

evidence.why: Separate scale-phase processing and mutating countdown helper.

facts.rationale: The existing false-path no-mutation claim contradicts the helper body. The corrected explanation distinguishes the activation countdown from appearance-phase progression.
facts.value: During parent state 0, calls it_8027A09C, which performs shared movement processing and tests pokemon_spawn.x24 before decrementing it. A positive countdown is decremented and returns false, so Ho-Oh stays in state 0 but the update is not mutation-free. A nonpositive countdown causes the helper to restore configured model scale and return true; the caller then performs common setup, enters state 1 with ITEM_ANIM_UPDATE, installs effect hitlag callbacks and sets xDD1_flag.b1. This activation guard is separate from the appearance-scale phase machine.

facts.rationale: Preserves the supported root-motion and transition flow while correcting the unsupported attack-flag interpretation using the generic consumer.
facts.value: Reads the Item and root JObj from the supplied object, selects the nullable first child and passes it with the Item to it_8027A160 for scaled animation-translation extraction. It then calls it_80272C6C on the object. A false result invokes it_802D2A58, which selects parent state 5, installs effect-hitlag and accessory callbacks, and sets xDCC_flag.b3. In generic item physics, b3 gates configured boundary-destruction checks; it is not established here as a damage or attack-enable flag.

evidence.why: Countdown activation and fixed-false collision wrapper.
Collision mutations and conditional callback/scale restoration.

facts.rationale: Retains verified collision behavior while correcting the stated cause of the separate activation transition.
facts.value: On parent state-0 collision updates, unconditionally delegates shared stage-collision processing through it_8027A118 and returns false. The shared routine copies collision position, conditionally records the floor index, combines collision-result flags and applies their shared responses. Its bit-1 path invokes the empty Ho-Oh callback and restores configured model scale. This collision callback does not request removal or select another state. The separate state-0 physics callback enters state 1 when the shared activation countdown is nonpositive, not by testing completion of the scale-phase machine.

evidence.why: Both selection spans and persisted line ID.
Selected-line movement applied to child position.

facts.rationale: Removes the beneath-only restriction contradicted by the constructor's fallback segment while retaining the supported Sacred Fire positioning role.
facts.value: Implements stage-relative positioning of Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire child by applying movement from the stage line selected during creation at Ho-Oh's saved release location. The selected line is not necessarily beneath that location: construction can fall back to a query spanning the top blast boundary down to the saved release height.
